claim: Let \(A=\{1,2,4,8\}\subset\mathbb Z\) and \(B=\{1,2,4,8,16,32,37,55,64\}\subset\mathbb Z/73\mathbb Z\). Among all cyclic \((73,9,1)\) perfect difference sets modulo \(73\), exactly one contains \(A\), namely \(B\); equivalently, exactly one affine image \(uB+v\) contains \(A\).

integrity.finite_checks: exact integer arithmetic; no floating-point computations

scientific_limitations: The theorem is specific to the seed \(A=\{1,2,4,8\}\) and modulus \(73\); it gives no result for other moduli.
Global uniqueness uses the published classification that all cyclic \((73,9,1)\) perfect difference sets lie in the Singer affine orbit.
The embedded checker verifies the finite orbit and containment calculations, but does not independently prove the published classification.
Independent audit and independent validation have not been performed.
title: Unique completion modulo 73 of a four-term Sidon seed
